author: greptile-apps
body:
Sync FK accesses in async function will raise SynchronousOnlyOperation
subscription.created_by and subscription.team are Django FK relations. If the Subscription object wasn't fetched with select_related('created_by', 'team'), accessing either attribute triggers a synchronous database query. In an async context (Temporal worker, asyncio event loop) that raises SynchronousOnlyOperation in Django 4.1+. The rest of the file correctly uses database_sync_to_async for ORM work (e.g. _resolve_slack_integration), but this function does not.
The fix is either to document a strict select_related contract on the caller side, or to load the relations explicitly before passing them down.
Prompt To Fix With AI

Line: 119-130

Comment:
**Sync FK accesses in async function will raise `SynchronousOnlyOperation`**

`subscription.created_by` and `subscription.team` are Django FK relations. If the `Subscription` object wasn't fetched with `select_related('created_by', 'team')`, accessing either attribute triggers a synchronous database query. In an async context (Temporal worker, asyncio event loop) that raises `SynchronousOnlyOperation` in Django 4.1+. The rest of the file correctly uses `database_sync_to_async` for ORM work (e.g. `_resolve_slack_integration`), but this function does not.

The fix is either to document a strict `select_related` contract on the caller side, or to load the relations explicitly before passing them down.

author: greptile-apps
body:
rendered_html parameter silently bypasses the sanitization stack
When a caller provides rendered_html, the nh3.clean() pass and _strip_external_links_markdown are both skipped, and the raw string is written into the Django template with {{ rendered_html|safe }}. Any future caller that passes pre-built HTML without running it through render_ai_email_html first would introduce an XSS path in the email output. Consider removing the bypass or at minimum adding a docstring warning that callers must only pass HTML already returned by render_ai_email_html.

author: veria-ai
body:
Medium: External URL stripping bypass
_strip_external_links_markdown only rewrites [text](url) and image syntax, then returns all other text unchanged. A report-content attacker can place https://attacker.example/<query-result> as a bare URL; the Slack delivery path sends it as mrkdwn and Slack will auto-unfurl it despite the PostHog-host allowlist. Run bare URLs/CommonMark autolinks through the same _is_allowed_link_url check before delivery, or disable Slack unfurls and remove external URL text from the report.

author: parameterai
body:
_BARE_URL_RE blind spot: parenthetical external URLs bypass Slack link defanging
The negative lookbehind in _BARE_URL_RE — (?<![(<@])— is designed to avoid re-processing the URL portion of an already-handledtextinline link. However, it equally skips any external URL that genuinely appears inside parenthetical text in the LLM synthesis output, e.g.The 'revenue (https://evil.com/t)' event spiked…`.
Attack chain: PostHog project tokens are often public in frontend JS, so an external visitor can fire events with arbitrary names like revenue (https://attacker.com/t). sanitize_user_text strips <…> HTML tags and LLM framing markers but has no rule for parenthetical URLs; the string passes through unchanged into the context blob (- Top events: revenue (https://attacker.com/t), …). If the synthesis LLM echoes the event name, _strip_external_links_markdown runs four passes and none catches it: _MARKDOWN_LINK_RE requires [text](url) syntax, _AUTOLINK_RE requires <url>, and _BARE_URL_RE fails the lookbehind because ( immediately precedes https://. In Slack delivery, mrkdwn text linkifies bare https:// URLs, creating a clickable link. unfurl=False prevents Slack's server-side auto-fetch (which was the main exfil channel), but the link remains clickable by the subscription owner. Email delivery is lower-impact because MarkdownIt without linkify does not hyperlink bare text URLs.

Prompt To Fix With AI
In `_BARE_URL_RE`, replace the single-character negative lookbehind `(?<![(<`@])` with a two-character lookbehind `(?<!\]\()` that specifically targets only the `[text](url)` markdown-link pattern (the actual case we want to skip). This allows parenthetical bare URLs like `(https://evil.com)` to be matched and defanged, while still not re-processing URLs that are the destination of an already-handled markdown link.

Change line 80 of `delivery.py`:
```python
# Before
_BARE_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![(<`@])((?:https?://|www\.)[^\s<>)\]`]+)")

# After – use a two-character fixed lookbehind to only skip the `](url)` markdown link context;
# add backtick lookahead guard separately to avoid double-wrapping a code span.
_BARE_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\]\()(?<![`@])((?:https?://|www\.)[^\s<>)\]`]+)")
```

Also add a regression test to `test_delivery.py`:
```python
def test_slack_defangs_parenthetical_external_url(self) -> None:
    # A URL inside parenthetical text must still be defanged even though it is preceded by '('
    message = _build_ai_slack_message(
        _mock_subscription(), "Revenue event (https://attacker.example/track) spiked."
    )
    all_text = " ".join(b["text"]["text"] for b in message.blocks if b["type"] == "section")
    assert "`https://attacker.example/track`" in all_text

def test_email_defangs_parenthetical_external_url(self) -> None:
    html = render_ai_email_html("Revenue event (https://attacker.example/track) spiked.")
    assert 'href="https://attacker.example' not in html
```



 Severity: low | Confidence: 65% 

Fixed in dbf7e510.

author: veria-ai
body:
Medium: External link allowlist bypass
urlparse(url).hostname treats URLs like https://attacker.example\@posthog.com/path as having hostname posthog.com, so _strip_external_links_markdown keeps the markdown link. Browsers and clients commonly treat the backslash as a path separator and navigate to attacker.example, letting prompt-injected report content deliver a live external phishing/exfil link despite the PostHog-only allowlist. Reject authority-bypass characters in the raw URL before parsing (there is already helper logic for this in posthog.api.utils) and require an https scheme before preserving the link.
